summary: Multi-org edition testing (backend + frontend). 26/26 backend pytest cases pass covering org CRUD, org isolation, org-link propose->approve->revoke, RBAC (user cannot mutate settings but can list + message + PTT), emergency ack toggle, cross-org dispatch guard, shift-log fan-out, and super_admin regression endpoints. Frontend login as super_admin works; TopBar shows DEFAULT+SUPER badge; SUPER_ADMIN role marker in operator strip; Orgs nav link visible; /admin/orgs renders (data-testid=superadmin-orgs), lists org cards with HB password + user-can-ack-emergency toggle; new-org-modal + new-org-link-modal open correctly; org-links-panel shows existing active link. Radio-detail dialog opens on roster double-click with z-index=2001 (correctly above map). PIN MESSAGES toggle activates persistent messages column. TX-active radio (TESTA_97973f) shows green highlight in roster. No blocking issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1700+ lines — consider splitting into routers (orgs, org-links, radios, messages, overlays) for maintainability.

tenancy.visible_org_ids returns an empty list [] as the 'no filter' sentinel for super_admin, then callers must additionally check role != 'super_admin' before treating [] as match-nothing. Current callers do it correctly via _user_visible_orgs which returns None for super_admin, but the dual sentinel (None vs []) is subtle and easy to misuse in future code.

Cross-org dispatch semantics could be documented in-line: to send to org B from org A, the link direction required is B->A (view+dispatch). Currently only surfaced via can_dispatch_org docstring — worth adding to API docs.
WebSocket connection warns 'closed before connection established' on initial page load but reconnects; not fatal but worth investigating for reliability.
